chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The salat of the two Eids with the Imam is a sunnah, and there is no salat before it nor after it on that day until noon.

So the proper way concerning this narration is that we understand his statement that it is a sunnah with the Imam to mean that its obligation was known through the sunnah, not that it is therefore non-obligatory. We have treated that fully in our major book, and we will devote a chapter to the fact that it is not obligatory except with the presence of the Imam.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the time of noon when the sun declines from its zenith
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam whose presence determines the ruling here
key_terms.بِحُضُورِ الْإِمَامِ: with the presence of the Imam
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: established through the sunnah; not necessarily non-obligatory in this context
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the prayer of the two Eids

ai.seo_question: Is Salat al-ʿĪdayn obligatory, and are there any prayers before or after it?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the salat of the two Eids, when performed with the Imam, is established through the sunnah and that no other salat is performed before or after it until noon on that day. The accompanying explanation clarifies that calling it a sunnah does not negate its obligatory nature in the appropriate circumstance, and that its obligation is tied to the presence of the Imam.
